title: Elastic Network Interfaces (ENI) and VPC attachment
hook: Every EC2 instance connects to your VPC through an Elastic Network Interface (ENI). The ENI owns the private IP, security groups, and subnet placement.

blocks.text: An Elastic Network Interface (ENI) is a virtual network card in a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) subnet. Each EC2 instance has a primary ENI (device index 0) created at launch. You can attach secondary ENIs for multi-homed designs, move ENIs between instances for failover, or assign multiple private IPv4 addresses and IPv6 addresses per ENI. Security groups attach to ENIs, not instances directly.

entries.plainDefinition: VPC virtual NIC with private IP, MAC, and security groups.
Device index 0 — deleted when instance terminates.

blocks.text: Lambda functions in a VPC create ENIs in subnets — scaling Lambda can exhaust IP addresses or ENI limits. Source/destination check must be disabled on firewalls and NAT instances so they can forward traffic. Misplaced ENI = wrong route table association and broken connectivity.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: ENI lives in one subnet, carries SGs and MAC address. Primary ENI defines instance network identity. Secondary ENI for traffic inspection or hot standby.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Create or launch
items.body: Primary ENI auto-created in selected subnet with primary private IP.

items.title: Attach secondary
items.body: Create ENI in target subnet, attach to running instance as eth1.

items.title: Apply security groups
items.body: Up to five SGs per ENI — stateful rules evaluate per ENI.

items.title: Route traffic
items.body: Subnet route table associated with ENI subnet determines egress path.

snippet.label: Create and attach secondary ENI
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-network-interface \
  --subnet-id subnet-data \
  --groups sg-inspect
aws ec2 attach-network-interface \
  --network-interface-id eni-0sec \
  --instance-id i-0app \
  --device-index 1
snippet.explanation: Secondary ENI can live in different subnet for inspection or management plane.

snippet.label: Disable source/dest check for NAT
snippet.explanation: Required when instance forwards packets between other hosts.

snippet.label: Launch template with multiple ENIs
snippet.code:
NetworkInterfaces:
  - DeviceIndex: 0
    SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetA
    Groups: [!Ref AppSecurityGroup]
  - DeviceIndex: 1
    SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetB
    Groups: [!Ref DataSecurityGroup]
snippet.explanation: Defines multi-homed instance at launch — avoids manual attach race at boot.

snippet.label: List ENIs for instance
snippet.explanation: First step when debugging wrong subnet or missing secondary ENI.

blocks.title: Runtime and deployment parallels
rows: ENI holds IP and MAC in VPC
Container has virtual eth inside task — like secondary ENI per task in awsvpc
App firewall in code — no VPC SG unless deployed on EC2/ECS
Detach ENI, attach to standby instance
Blue/green by redeploying container to new host
No ENI concept on Lambda outside VPC

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Forgetting Lambda in VPC consumes subnet IPs via ENIs. Leaving source/dest check enabled on a routing appliance. Attaching ENI in subnet without available IPs.

blocks.text: Hyperplane ENIs reduced Lambda cold start for VPC functions but still plan IP capacity (/28 subnets exhaust fast). How to prove it in production: describe-network-interfaces filtered by description "AWS Lambda" for IP burn rate; VPC Reachability Analyzer for path through multi-ENI appliance.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Manual or scripted — not automatic like Multi-AZ RDS
Host many TLS certs or containers
Lower latency P99 on supported instances

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying security groups attach to EC2 instances — they attach to ENIs. Strong answer: primary ENI subnet sets route table; SG is stateful per ENI; Lambda VPC mode creates ENIs.

interviewTakeaways: ENI is the VPC network identity — subnet, private IP, MAC, and security groups.
Primary ENI is created with the instance; secondary ENIs enable multi-homed and failover patterns.
Disable source/dest check only on routing/NAT appliances — not ordinary app servers.
60s: ENI in one subnet, SGs on ENI. Primary at launch. Lambda VPC burns ENIs and IPs. Source/dest off for routers only.
Follow-up: how does Lambda ENI scaling affect subnet sizing?
commonPitfalls: Saying SG attaches to instance — rejected; SG attaches to ENI.
Strong answer: check ENI subnet route table and SG for each interface separately.
/28 subnet for Lambda without calculating ENI peak concurrency.
Moving ENI without updating OS network config on Linux secondary interface.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node server binds 0.0.0.0 on all interfaces — on multi-ENI EC2, ensure traffic hits correct SG by binding specific private IP.
Lambda in VPC is like a headless function with hidden ENIs — unlike a long-running Express server you SSH into.
